messages:
alex: Quick cost sweep — we need a recommendation on region placement for inference committed capacity vs. on-demand. Pulled last 30d cloud billing and utilization. TL;DR: centralize where it saves $$ but keep latency for EU/APAC.
ben: Raw numbers from the billing export (rounded):
```
region         reserved $/GPUh   on-demand $/GPUh   avg util   egress $/GB
us-west1       0.78             1.20               72%        0.09
europe-west1   0.94             1.45               68%        0.11
ap-southeast1  1.28             1.62               45%        0.18
```
Notes: reserved = 12mo commit pricing we can buy today. APAC on-demand high partly due to smaller instance SKUs and egress.
maria: Latency/SLAs: p50 to EU customers from us-west is ~60ms, p95 ~120ms for chat paths — still within SLO for most products, but embeddings search is more latency sensitive (p95 goal <100ms).
ravi: Inventory update — APAC reserved SKU availability is low for next 8–12 weeks for our preferred GPU type (A10G). If we want reserve in APAC we may need to switch sku (tradeoff: perf) or wait.
suzanne: Also consider cross-region egress and interconnect costs if we centralize models. We saw a 25% bump last month when a routing change sent more traffic to us-west; that's ~+$30k.
billing-bot: Spreadsheet with per-cluster breakdown + model token breakdown: https://redwood.internal/sheets/regional-costs-30d (view-only link) :link:
alex: If we commit, where gives highest ROI? Quick calc: assume 70% util sustained, 12mo commit — us-west ROI ~35% cost reduction vs on-demand; eu-west ~33%; apac only ~18% due to lower util and higher base price + egress.
ben: Recommendation draft:
- Commit in us-west1 for core inference fleet (24 GPUs) — highest utilization, lowest unit price.
- Commit in europe-west1 smaller pool (12 GPUs) for EU-first customers and to cut egress.
- No APAC commit for now; use small reserved hot-cache (4 GPUs) via Dedicated on-demand burst + investigate local partner/marketplaces for cheaper APAC capacity.
- Keep ability to burst to on-demand in apac for seasonal spikes.
maria: +1 but we must pin embeddings heavy customers to eu-west when they’re EU-only to avoid egress and data residency. Also consider canary shift of a small traffic slice to eu commit before fully routing.
ravi: Ops constraints: provisioning 24 GPUs in us-west will require a small infra change (nodegroups + autoscaler tune). ETA ~2 weeks once purchase is approved. APAC fallback: we can pre-approve a cross-region burst policy to avoid throttling.
suzanne: Risk: committing too much in europe could lead to idle capacity if EU feature adoption stalls. Suggest 6mo trial for eu commit, 12mo for us-west. Also require a rollback budget for early termination (~10% penalty typical).
alex: Okay action items: 1) Finance to approve 12mo us-west commit for 24 GPUs (ben to own). 2) Purchase 6mo europe commit for 12 GPUs as trial (suzanne to present penalty table). 3) Ops to prepare provisioning runbook and autoscaler changes (ravi). 4) Product/edge: pin EU customers & run a 2-week canary to eu commit (maria).
billing-bot: Created ticket FIN-3245 for commit approvals and attached pricing terms.
ben: I'll assemble a final ROI spreadsheet with sensitivity to util (60/70/80%) and post it here by EOD.
alex: Sounds good. If we can shave egress by 0.03–0.05 $/GB via peering in EU we should re-run numbers — that flips the 6mo vs 12mo decision.
maria: I'll follow up with network to check peering oppty.
ravi: I'll start infra PR template for the nodegroup changes, link when ready.
suzanne: +1 on phased approach. If anyone sees a region-specific promo from a cloud partner (credits or marketplace SKUs) drop it here.
alex: Thanks team — plan: ben + finance to push purchase, ravi + ops to prep infra, maria + product to coordinate routing canary. Revisit in 48h. :white_check_mark:
